existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: No hard R4→R6 instance break was found for local `NamingSystem` fields. The top concerns are lossless R6→R4 downgrade of new metadata, enum/validator handling for new `uniqueId.type` codes, and semantic review for jurisdiction and lifecycle metadata. The main uncertainty is terminology expansion detail for external terminology.hl7.org bindings.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Existing R4 instances should generally validate structurally in R6 after normal version handling, but R6 instances are richer than R4 can natively represent. Migration tooling should preserve R6-only canonical and governance metadata through official cross-version extensions, sidecar metadata, or an R6-native store rather than silently dropping it. Terminology code paths should update generated enums and validation tables for `namingsystem-identifier-type`, and business rules should review `jurisdiction`, `date`, `purpose`, `approvalDate`, `lastReviewDate`, and `effectivePeriod` rather than assuming R4 semantics.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural/cardinality/type comparisons because both assigned StructureDefinitions are present locally and were compared through snapshot and differential elements. Confidence is high for the `uniqueId.type`, `kind`, and `status` code-list comparisons where complete local CodeSystems are present. Confidence is medium for extensible/preferred and external terminology bindings because no live expansion service or official narrative diff was available.

2 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.
